66920-keeping-down-the-cost-of-your-wood.title: Keeping Down The Cost Of Your Woodwork
66920-keeping-down-the-cost-of-your-wood.creator: Unknown
66920-keeping-down-the-cost-of-your-wood.description: A public-domain book from Project Gutenberg. “lower costs?” Curtis Woodwork is not the lowest priced woodwork on the market, but it is the greatest value, dollar for dollar. You may be able to buy, for less money, woodwork that looks something like Curtis material. Cheaper material cannot, of course, have the same quality as Curtis Woodwork all the way through. arxiv-1908-07662.title: Assessment of protein assembly prediction in CASP13
arxiv-1908-07662.creator: Dmytro Guzenko, Aleix Lafita, Bohdan Monastyrskyy, Andriy Kryshtafovych, Jose M. Duarte
arxiv-1908-07662.description: Abstract We present the assembly category assessment in the 13 th edition of the CASP community-wide experiment. For the second time, protein assemblies constitute an independent assessment category. Compared to the last edition we see a clear uptake in participation, more oligomeric targets released, and consistent, albeit modest, improvement of the predictions quality.

arxiv-2109-00810.title: Evaluating the Single-Shot MultiBox Detector and YOLO Deep Learning Models for the Detection of Tomatoes in a Greenhouse
arxiv-2109-00810.creator: Sandro Augusto Magalhães *, Luís Castro, Germano Moreira, Filipe Neves dos Santos *, Mário Cunha, Jorge Dias, António Paulo Moreira \orcidG
arxiv-2109-00810.description: Abstract The development of robotic solutions for agriculture requires advanced perception capabilities that can work reliably in any crop stage. For example, to automatise the tomato harvesting process in greenhouses, the visual perception system needs to detect the tomato in any life cycle stage (flower to the ripe tomato).

arxiv-2206-11360.title: Computing transition path theory quantities with trajectory stratification
arxiv-2206-11360.creator: Bodhi P. Vani, Jonathan Weare, Aaron R. Dinner ∗
arxiv-2206-11360.description: A 2022 arXiv research paper by Bodhi P. Vani, Jonathan Weare, Aaron R. Dinner ∗. Transition path theory computes statistics from ensembles of reactive trajectories. A common strategy for sampling reactive trajectories is to control the branching and pruning of trajectories so as to enhance the sampling of low probability segments. However, it can be challenging to apply transition path theory to data from such methods because determining whether configurations and trajectory segments are part of reactive trajectories requires looking backward and forward in time.

arxiv-2210-02479.title: A Systematic View of Ten New Black Hole Spins
arxiv-2210-02479.creator: Paul A. Draghis, Jon M. Miller, Abderahmen Zoghbi, Mark Reynolds, Elisa Costantini, Luigi C. Gallo, John A. Tomsick
arxiv-2210-02479.description: Abstract The launch of NuSTAR and the increasing number of binary black hole (BBH) mergers detected through gravitational wave (GW) observations have exponentially advanced our understanding of black holes. Despite the simplicity owed to being fully described by their mass and angular momentum, black holes have remained mysterious laboratories that probe the most extreme environments in the Universe.

arxiv-2309-11906.title: On the kernel of SO ⁡ ( 3 ) \mathrm{SO}(3) -Witten-Reshetikhin-Turaev quantum representations
arxiv-2309-11906.creator: Renaud Detcherry, Ramanujan Santharoubane
arxiv-2309-11906.description: A 2023 arXiv research paper by Renaud Detcherry, Ramanujan Santharoubane. In this paper, we study the kernels of the SO ⁡ ( 3 ) \mathrm{SO}(3) -Witten-Reshetikhin-Turaev quantum representations ρ p \rho_{p} of mapping class groups of closed orientable surfaces Σ g \Sigma_{g} of genus g . We investigate the question whether the kernel of ρ p \rho_{p} for p p prime is exactly the subgroup generated by p p -th powers of Dehn twists.

arxiv-2408-09066.title: Brain Inspired Probabilistic Occupancy Grid Mapping with Vector Symbolic Architectures
arxiv-2408-09066.creator: Shay Snyder, Andrew Capodieci, David Gorsich, Maryam Parsa
arxiv-2408-09066.description: A 2024 arXiv research paper by Shay Snyder, Andrew Capodieci, David Gorsich, Maryam Parsa. Real-time robotic systems require advanced perception, computation, and action capability. However, the main bottleneck in current autonomous systems is the trade-off between computational capability, energy efficiency and model determinism. World modeling, a key objective of many robotic systems, commonly uses occupancy grid mapping (OGM) as the first step towards building an end-to-end robotic system with perception, planning, autonomous maneuvering, and decision making capabilities.

arxiv-2503-23042.title: MIL vs. Aggregation: Evaluating Patient-Level Survival Prediction Strategies Using Graph-Based Learning
arxiv-2503-23042.creator: Maria Rita Verdelho, Alexandre Bernardino, Catarina Barata
arxiv-2503-23042.description: Abstract Oncologists often rely on a multitude of data, including whole-slide images (WSIs), to guide therapeutic decisions, aiming for the best patient outcome. However, predicting the prognosis of cancer patients can be a challenging task due to tumor heterogeneity and intra-patient variability, and the complexity of analyzing WSIs.

arxiv-2509-04667.title: DarkStream: real-time speech anonymization with low latency
arxiv-2509-04667.creator: Waris Quamer, Ricardo Gutierrez-Osuna
arxiv-2509-04667.description: Abstract We propose DarkStream, a streaming speech synthesis model for real-time speaker anonymization. To improve content encoding under strict latency constraints, DarkStream combines a causal waveform encoder, a short lookahead buffer, and transformer-based contextual layers. To further reduce inference time, the model generates waveforms directly via a neural vocoder, thus removing intermediate mel-spectrogram conversions.

arxiv-2512-12691.title: Effects of radiative interior on solar inertial modes
arxiv-2512-12691.creator: Suprabha Mukhopadhyay, Yuto Bekki, Xiaojue Zhu, Laurent Gizon
arxiv-2512-12691.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Suprabha Mukhopadhyay, Yuto Bekki, Xiaojue Zhu, Laurent Gizon. The solar inertial modes are expected to play important diagnostic and dynamical roles in the Sun’s differentially rotating convection zone. The coupling of these modes to the radiative interior is yet to be discussed. We aim to understand the dependence of the modes on the uniformly rotating subadiabatic region below the convection zone, and whether this leads to measurable changes at the surface.

arxiv-2512-19728.title: Hard Negative Sample–Augmented DPO Post-Training for Small Language Models
arxiv-2512-19728.creator: Haocheng Lu hl5026@nyu.edu, Minjun Zhu mz3487@nyu.edu, Henry Yu ky2389@nyu.edu
arxiv-2512-19728.description: Abstract Large language models (LLMs) continue to struggle with mathematical reasoning, and common post-training pipelines often reduce each generated solution to a binary outcome: correct or incorrect. This view is limiting in practice, because failures in chain-of-thought (CoT) reasoning are frequently structured —solutions may look convincing while containing subtle logical, algebraic, or numerical flaws.

pmc-11388168.title: Modulation of CB1 cannabinoid receptor alters the electrophysiological properties of cerebellar Purkinje cells in harmaline-induced essential tremor
pmc-11388168.creator: Hassan Abbassian, Mehran Ilaghi, Reza Saboori Amleshi, Benjamin Jason Whalley, Mohammad Shabani
pmc-11388168.description: Essential tremor (ET) is one of the most common motor disorders with debilitating effects on the affected individuals. The endocannabinoid system is widely involved in cerebellar signaling. Therefore, modulation of cannabinoid-1 receptors (CB1Rs) has emerged as a novel target for motor disorders.

pmc-11577689.title: Bayesian blockwise inference for joint models of longitudinal and multistate data with application to longitudinal multimorbidity analysis
pmc-11577689.creator: Sida Chen, Danilo Alvares, Christopher Jackson, Tom Marshall, Krish Nirantharakumar, Sylvia Richardson, Catherine L Saunders, Jessica K Barrett
pmc-11577689.description: Multistate models provide a useful framework for modelling complex event history data in clinical settings and have recently been extended to the joint modelling framework to appropriately handle endogenous longitudinal covariates, such as repeatedly measured biomarkers, which are informative about health status and disease progression. However, the practical application of such joint models faces considerable computational challenges.

pmc-12484180.title: Sub-chronic stress exerts partially distinct behavioral and epigenetic effects in male and female mice
pmc-12484180.creator: Matthew J. Domanico, Sophie Stevens, Iris Wainston, Emily Khoo, Corey McCall, Benjamin D. Swack, Benjamin D. Sachs
pmc-12484180.description: IntroductionStress-related disorders, such as major depression, anxiety disorders, and post-traumatic stress disorder, lead to considerable disease burden and are notoriously difficult to treat. These disorders are characterized by striking sex differences, but the neurobiological underpinnings of the disparities in mental health between men and women remain largely undefined.

pmc-12594847.title: Cinchona-based liquid formulation exhibits antifungal activity through Tryptophan starvation and disruption of mitochondrial respiration in Rhizoctonia Solani
pmc-12594847.creator: Simanta Das, Srinjoy Ghosh, Kumaresh Pal, Moumita Chakraborty, Surajit Khalko, Sk. Masudul Islam, Samuel Rai, Ashok Choudhury, Nandita Sahana, Somnath Mandal
pmc-12594847.description: This study investigates the antifungal properties of a liquid Cinchona-Based Formulation (CBF) against Rhizoctonia solani. CBF, a stable acidic extract of Cinchona bark (0.1 N HCl), effectively suppressed mycelial growth (58.75 ± 0.48%) and sclerotia biomass (22.1 ± 0.65 mg), with an EC50 of 217.14 µg/mL. GC-MS and HPLC revealed quinine as the primary active alkaloid.

pmc-13204631.title: Efficacy and Safety of Oral NEPA Versus Fosaprepitant Plus Palonosetron for Preventing Chemotherapy-Induced Nausea and Vomiting in Patients with Nasopharyngeal Carcinoma: A Propensity-Score-Matched Retrospective Study
pmc-13204631.creator: Yilin Cai, Ying Zeng, Qihang Li, Guihua Yi, Donghong Yang, Tongyuan Deng, Xiangyong Li, Haiqing Luo
pmc-13204631.description: Simple SummaryPatients with nasopharyngeal carcinoma often receive cisplatin-based chemotherapy, which causes severe nausea and vomiting. Standard antiemetic regimens are effective but complicated to administer. This study compared a single oral capsule containing netupitant and palonosetron with a standard intravenous two-drug regimen.

pmc-13332134.title: Optimizing Broiler Diets: Nutritional and Functional Benefits of Fermented Cottonseed Meal
pmc-13332134.creator: Dan Song, Qiuxi Xuan, Beibei He, Xiaolin Hou, Yongwei Wang, Weiwei Wang, Kuanbo Liu, Tao Duan, Junlin Cheng, Aike Li, Lin Qiao
pmc-13332134.description: Cottonseed meal (CSM) contains antinutritional factors limiting its use. Fermentation may improve its nutritional value. This study examined the nutritional properties of fermented cottonseed meal (FCSM) and its effects on broilers. The nutritional composition of fermented CSM and FCSM was analyzed.

pmc-13478344.title: Fractal hierarchy enables exponential scaling of topological boundary states
pmc-13478344.creator: Limin Song, Zhichan Hu, Ziteng Wang, Domenico Bongiovanni, Liqin Tang, Daohong Song, Roberto Morandotti, Jingjun Xu, Hrvoje Buljan, Zhigang Chen
pmc-13478344.description: Exponential growth describes an extremely rapid process ubiquitous in mathematics and across diverse physical, biological, and technological systems. Here, we introduce a class of fractal-inspired lattices that combine long-range periodic order with self-similar hierarchy, establishing a structural motif that enables exponential scaling of topological boundary states.

pmc-13570963.creator: Shadman M. Rahman, Allison Peng, Kristen Si, Carys L. Kenny-Howell, Mantej Singh, Muhammad Ahsan Asif, Saumik Z. Rahman, Saeed Rahmani, Luca Pasquini, Mehmet Adin, Elizabeth Schrickel, Long H. Tu
